assumptions: Movement is bilateral and counted in repetitions.
Feet are anchored, so the hip flexors work with the feet fixed (closed chain).
Hands stay at the head or ears without pulling on the neck, so no cervical action is modeled.
Lumbar spine flexion represents trunk flexion; no thoracic spine joint exists in the vocabulary.
Hands are only placed at the head, so grip and wrist stability are not required.
Anchored feet give no meaningful stabilizing load at the ankles, and no stabilization demand is added for the bodyweight trunk work.
classification_reasons: Instructions and frames show a bilateral bodyweight sit-up with feet anchored under a dumbbell, hands at the head, and the torso curling and flexing the hips to reach roughly vertical.
The exertion phase is spinal flexion plus hip flexion, and both actions are in the vocabulary.
Only the range is partial (three-quarters of the way down), which does not change the joint actions.

instructions: Lie down on the floor and secure your feet. Your legs should be bent at the knees.
Place your hands behind or to the side of your head. You will begin with your back on the ground. This will be your starting position.
Flex your hips and spine to raise your torso toward your knees.
At the top of the contraction your torso should be perpendicular to the ground. Reverse the motion, going only ¾ of the way down.
Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.
